properties.name: Cafe by the Ruins
properties.description: A beloved institution serving Cordillera-inspired dishes, tapuy rice wine, and rustic bread beside the old ruins downtown. Its garden-fresh cooking helped define Baguio's slow-food identity.

properties.name: Hill Station
properties.description: A candle-lit restaurant inside historic Casa Vallejo blending Filipino, Spanish, and Asian flavors along old trade routes. Its refined plates and cozy interiors make it a favorite for special evenings.

properties.name: Good Taste Cafe and Restaurant
properties.description: A cavernous, always-open eatery famous for enormous portions of buttered chicken and fried rice at rock-bottom prices. It is the go-to refuel stop for hungry travelers at any hour.

properties.name: Oh My Gulay
properties.description: An artist-run vegetarian cafe crowning the La Azotea building, filled with whimsical installations and a koi pond. Its meat-free plates and creative ambience draw students and bohemians alike.

properties.name: 50's Diner
properties.description: A nostalgic American-style diner on Leonard Wood Road serving hearty breakfasts, burgers, and thick milkshakes. Its jukebox decor and generous plates make it a long-running local favorite.

properties.name: Canto Bogchi Joint
properties.description: A casual grill renowned for its tender rib platters and comforting rice bowls. Locals prize it as one of the city's best-value comfort-food stops.

properties.name: Amare La Cucina
properties.description: A cozy trattoria turning out wood-fired Neapolitan pizzas and hearty pasta in the cool mountain air. Its authentic Italian fare has earned a devoted following.

properties.name: Lemon and Olives Greek Taverna
properties.description: The city's only Greek taverna, perched on Outlook Drive with sweeping ridge views and authentic Mediterranean plates. Its souvlaki and moussaka offer a sunlit change of pace.

properties.name: Ketchup Food Community
properties.description: A cluster of independent eateries sharing a pine-shaded compound on Romulo Drive near Wright Park. Diners can graze across Filipino, Mexican, and grilled specialties in one leafy setting.

properties.name: Vizco's Restaurant and Cake Shop
properties.description: A Session Road bakeshop famed for its towering strawberry shortcake made with fresh Benguet berries. Its cakes are among the city's most popular edible pasalubong.

properties.name: Good Shepherd Convent Store
properties.description: The convent store beside Mines View selling the nuns' celebrated ube halaya, strawberry jam, and peanut brittle. Every jar funds scholarships for Cordillera students.

properties.name: Baguio Country Club Bakeshop
properties.description: The historic club's bakeshop, whose warm raisin bread is a legendary Baguio pasalubong. Visitors line up for loaves fresh from the oven.

properties.name: Choco-late de Batirol
properties.description: A garden cafe in Camp John Hay serving thick native tsokolate whisked the traditional way with a batirol. Its cozy nipa huts pair the drink with Filipino rice cakes.

properties.name: Mines View Souvenir Row
properties.description: The dense stretch of stalls beside Mines View Park brimming with knitted bonnets, wooden crafts, and trinkets. It is the classic spot for last-minute Baguio keepsakes.

properties.name: Easter Weaving Room
properties.description: A century-old weaving center in Guisad where visitors watch artisans work traditional looms. Its handwoven Cordillera textiles, bags, and blankets support local weavers.

properties.name: Ibay's Silver Shop
properties.description: A long-established silversmith crafting jewelry inspired by Cordillera patterns and symbols. Its handmade rings and pendants are treasured Baguio mementos.

properties.name: Narda's Handwoven Arts and Crafts
properties.description: A pioneering weaving house whose ikat-dyed shawls and garments carry Cordillera craft into contemporary fashion. Its refined pieces are gifted and worn nationwide.

properties.name: Public Market Pasalubong Stalls
properties.description: The pasalubong section of the public market packed with strawberry preserves, highland coffee, and native brooms. It is the most affordable place to stock up on Baguio treats.

properties.name: The Manor at Camp John Hay
properties.description: The flagship luxury hotel of Camp John Hay, styled like a grand alpine lodge amid towering pines. Its log-and-stone interiors and cozy fireplaces epitomize upscale mountain retreat.

properties.name: Forest Lodge at Camp John Hay
properties.description: A comfortable pine-side lodge within Camp John Hay offering easy access to the golf course and trails. Its warm rooms suit families and groups seeking a forest escape.

properties.name: Hotel Elizabeth Baguio
properties.description: A gracious mid-range hotel on Gibraltar Road with colonial-inspired decor and a well-regarded restaurant. Its quiet ridge location is close to Mines View and Wright Park.

properties.name: Microtel by Wyndham Baguio
properties.description: A dependable upper-Session hotel offering clean, comfortable rooms with sweeping views over the downtown bowl. Its central location puts the market and Burnham Park within easy reach.

properties.name: Baguio Country Club
properties.description: A prestigious members' club and hotel dating to 1905, set on manicured grounds beside a historic golf course. Its heritage halls and famous bakeshop make it a Baguio landmark in their own right.

properties.name: Casa Vallejo
properties.description: The city's oldest surviving hotel, a 1909 wooden landmark at the top of Session Road with creaking floors and vintage charm. It shares its walls with an indie cinema, bookshop, and Hill Station restaurant.

properties.name: Azalea Residences Baguio
properties.description: An apartment-style hotel on Leonard Wood Loop offering suites with kitchenettes for longer family stays. Its quiet residential setting is a short ride from downtown attractions.

properties.name: Pine Breeze Transient House
properties.description: A budget transient home in Aurora Hill with roomy shared quarters popular among student and family groups. Guests cook their own meals and enjoy a homey mountain base.

properties.name: Cordillera Family Transient
properties.description: A homey Guisad transient house rented whole for reunions and barkada trips. Its full kitchen and living room give large groups an affordable home away from home.

properties.name: Session Road Backpackers
properties.description: A compact hostel steps from Session Road offering bunk beds and a sociable common lounge. Its central spot suits solo travelers exploring the downtown core on foot.

properties.name: Mountain View Transient
properties.description: A simple transient house on Gibraltar Road with balconies framing the eastern mountains. Its proximity to Mines View makes it a convenient budget base for sightseeing.

properties.name: Strawberry Fields Transient
properties.description: A quiet transient house on the La Trinidad edge, minutes from the famous strawberry fields. It offers groups a restful, low-cost stay away from the downtown bustle.
